skill.name: github-automation
skill.description: Automate GitHub repositories, issues, pull requests, branches, CI/CD workflows, permissions, and code search through Rube MCP GitHub tools.
skill.summary: Automates GitHub repository, issue, pull request, CI/CD, and permission workflows through Rube MCP.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick findings are false positives because SKILL.md uses Markdown inline code for tool names and parameters, not executable shell syntax. The skill does require an external Rube MCP endpoint and includes high-impact GitHub administration workflows, so consent and permission safeguards are important. No evidence of prompt injection or hidden credential exfiltration was found.

remediation.suggestion: Clearly document that GitHub data and actions route through Rube MCP, and require users to review the OAuth connection before use.
Keep explicit confirmation gates for merge, delete, workflow dispatch, branch protection, and collaborator changes. Show the target repository and action before execution.

static_findings.snippet: - Active GitHub connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `github`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
- `GITHUB_LIST_REPOSITORY_ISSUES` returns both issues AND pull requests; check `pull_request` field
- Pagination: `per_page` max 100; iterate pages until empty
2. `GITHUB_GET_A_PULL_REQUEST` - Get detailed PR info including mergeable status [Required]
- `head`: Source branch with changes (must exist; for cross-repo: 'username:branch')
- `GITHUB_CREATE_A_PULL_REQUEST` fails with 422 if base/head are invalid, identical, or already merg
- `GITHUB_MERGE_A_PULL_REQUEST` can be rejected if PR is draft, closed, or branch protection applies
- Always verify mergeable status with `GITHUB_GET_A_PULL_REQUEST` immediately before merging
- `sha`: Commit SHA to point the new reference to
- `GITHUB_CREATE_A_REFERENCE` only creates NEW references; use `GITHUB_UPDATE_A_REFERENCE` for exist
- `ref` must start with 'refs/' and contain at least two slashes
- `GITHUB_LIST_BRANCHES` paginates via `page`/`per_page`; iterate until empty page
- `GITHUB_DELETE_A_REPOSITORY` is permanent and irreversible; requires admin privileges
4. `GITHUB_LIST_COMMITS` - List commits for a specific repo [Alternative]
- `GITHUB_SEARCH_COMMITS_BY_AUTHOR` requires keywords in addition to qualifiers; qualifier-only quer
2. `GITHUB_GET_A_WORKFLOW` - Get workflow details by ID or filename [Optional]
4. `GITHUB_LIST_CHECK_RUNS_FOR_A_REF` - Check CI status for a commit/branch [Required]
- `inputs`: JSON string of workflow inputs matching `on.workflow_dispatch.inputs`
- `GITHUB_CREATE_A_WORKFLOW_DISPATCH_EVENT` requires the workflow to have `workflow_dispatch` trigge
- Full path `.github/workflows/main.yml` is auto-stripped to just `main.yml`
- Inputs max 10 key-value pairs; must match workflow's `on.workflow_dispatch.inputs` definitions
- `GITHUB_GET_BRANCH_PROTECTION` returns 404 for unprotected branches; treat as no protection rules
- Determine push ability from `permissions.push` or `role_name`, not display labels
- Iterate until response returns fewer results than `per_page`
- Check CI status with `GITHUB_LIST_CHECK_RUNS_FOR_A_REF` before merging
- **Issues vs PRs**: `GITHUB_LIST_REPOSITORY_ISSUES` returns both; check `pull_request` field
- **Pagination limits**: `per_page` max 100; always iterate pages until empty
- **Branch creation**: `GITHUB_CREATE_A_REFERENCE` fails with 422 if reference already exists
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k

content.value_statement: GitHub administration often requires many repeated checks across repositories, pull requests, issues, and CI/CD status. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Rube MCP GitHub workflows.
actual_capabilities: Connects through Rube MCP and checks the active GitHub tool schemas before running workflows.
Creates, lists, searches, and comments on GitHub issues across accessible repositories.
Finds, creates, reviews, and merges pull requests after checking mergeability and CI status.
Creates repositories and branches, updates repository settings, and handles reference operations.
Searches code, commits, and repository content with GitHub query qualifiers and pagination guidance.
Lists workflows, deployments, collaborators, permissions, and branch protection settings.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP and an active GitHub OAuth connection before any workflow can run.
Cannot bypass GitHub permissions, branch protection rules, or repository visibility limits.
Depends on current Rube MCP tool schemas and GitHub API pagination or search limits.
Destructive or privileged actions still require careful user review before execution.

use_cases.title: Triage Repository Issues
use_cases.description: Find open issues, separate pull requests from issues, add comments, and prepare labels or assignees for accessible repositories.

use_cases.title: Review Pull Requests
use_cases.description: Inspect pull request details, changed files, mergeability, and check runs before deciding whether to merge.

use_cases.title: Audit Repository Access
use_cases.description: List collaborators, inspect permissions, review branch protection, and identify settings that need follow-up.

prompt_templates.title: List My Repositories
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the GitHub automation skill to list my accessible repositories. Show names, visibility, default branch, and recent activity.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitHub issue in OWNER/REPO titled TITLE with this description: DESCRIPTION. Confirm the target repository before creating it.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Pull Request
prompt_templates.prompt: Review pull request NUMBER in OWNER/REPO. Check changed files, mergeability, branch protection, and CI status. Summarize risks before any action.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit OWNER/REPO for release readiness. Review open pull requests, failing checks, recent deployments, workflows, collaborators, and branch protection gaps.

output_examples.output: The response summarizes the pull request state, changed files, mergeability, check run status, and branch protection blockers. It asks for explicit approval before merging.

output_examples.input: Find issues about login failures in my repositories.
output_examples.output: The response lists matching issues by repository, title, status, labels, assignees, and update time. Pull requests are separated from issues.

output_examples.input: Audit repository permissions for the platform team.
output_examples.output: The response reports collaborator roles, branch protection status, and any permission changes that need manual confirmation.

best_practices: Call Rube tool discovery first so requests use the current GitHub tool schemas.
Verify repository owner, repository name, branch, and pull request number before privileged actions.
Check mergeability, CI status, and branch protection immediately before merging or changing settings.
anti_patterns: Do not merge pull requests, delete repositories, or change permissions without explicit user approval.
Do not assume issue results exclude pull requests; check the pull request marker first.
Do not stop at the first page when listing repositories, issues, collaborators, or branches.

faq.question: Does this skill need a GitHub token?
faq.answer: It uses a GitHub OAuth connection through Rube MCP. The user must connect GitHub before workflows can run.

faq.question: Can it create pull requests?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide pull request creation when the source branch, target branch, title, and repository are known.

faq.question: Can it merge pull requests automatically?
faq.answer: It can call the merge tool, but the skill instructs agents to require explicit user confirmation first.

faq.question: Can it delete repositories?
faq.answer: The skill warns that repository deletion is permanent and requires admin privileges. Users should treat deletion as a manual approval action.

faq.question: Does it support GitHub Actions?
faq.answer: Yes. It can list workflows, inspect workflow details, trigger dispatch events, and check run status for a reference.

faq.question: What are the main limits?
faq.answer: GitHub permissions, branch protection, Rube tool availability, pagination, and GitHub search limits define what the skill can complete.
